A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FINC research, despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original FINC clustering results, mode-frequency estimates, unseen-sample scores, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports controlled colored-data experiments and a Kinetics-400/UCF101 comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains Gaussian random Fourier features, covariance accumulation, the covariance difference, and spectral decomposition. The mode-scoring function is also unchanged. Different experimental embeddings do not introduce a new FINC procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds colored MNIST and Fashion-MNIST scenarios and extends evaluation to video through Kinetics-400 versus UCF101. These introduce controlled visual novelty and another data modality. Existing ImageNet, AFHQ, FFHQ/CelebA, and MS-COCO coverage remains represented across the main text and appendices.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Rarity plus spectral clustering, FLD plus spectral clustering, and KEN with eigen-decomposition or Cholesky decomposition. Corresponding qualitative comparisons retain the same comparator membership. The newly added dataset checks introduce no additional baseline methods.

E3.justification: Several main image comparisons report DINOv2 instead of Inception-V3 embeddings. New protocols use disjoint, partly colorized datasets with raw-pixel features and video evaluation with I3D features; the feature-count sweep also drops r=500. Exact AFHQ sampling remains unclear because v2 Figure 7 claims 50k FINC samples despite the retained 15k-dataset description.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds controlled sanity checks asking whether FINC recovers known colored classes when grayscale test samples are also unseen. These extend the existing real-dataset sanity checks. The bandwidth-sensitivity, alternative-feature-extractor, and unseen-sample analyses are retained, largely through relocation.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 3 reports mode frequencies with ± uncertainty for AFHQ/ImageNet-dogs and FFHQ/CelebA. Those summaries disappear, and v2's replacement AFHQ display is purely qualitative. The StyleGAN-XL uncertainty annotations remain unchanged in v2 Figure 19. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or explains the ± estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds colored-data and video findings and replaces several ImageNet/LDM qualitative results. For example, LDM's leading overrepresented mode changes from boats in v1 Figure 2 to koalas in v2 Figure 4; changed embeddings prevent a direct performance comparison. v1 Figure 3's frequencies disappear, while Table 1 and relocated StyleGAN-XL frequencies and unseen-sample scores remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the matrix square-root perturbation step in v1 Equation 8, now v2 Equation 9. The introductory feature-count bound is aligned with the existing epsilon^-4 theorem. Theorem 1 otherwise remains equivalent; its squared-bound presentation does not introduce a new guarantee.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the advertised random-feature requirement from O(log n/epsilon^2) to O(log n/epsilon^4), weakening its stated accuracy dependence to match Theorem 1. The central contributions—differential clustering, scalable FINC, approximation guarantees, and generative-model comparisons—retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific limitation that clustering depends on embedding quality and may work less satisfactorily outside vision. Section 5.2 also newly interprets LDM's model-to-model frequency differences as moderately consistent with its overrepresentation relative to ImageNet. Existing bandwidth and feature-extractor interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a FINC code-repository link and Appendix B.6 specifying PyTorch, dual 24-core CPUs, 500 GB memory, and eight RTX 3090 GPUs. It also documents the new video's 1024-dimensional I3D representation. These expand reproducibility information without establishing that retained timing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds CLIP, DINOv2, and video-dataset/evaluation references, removes the Inception-architecture reference, and adds discussion positioning embedding choice against evaluation bias. The established relationship to random Fourier features, differential clustering, and KEN is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and opening motivation are rewritten, Section 5.2 gains explanatory subheadings, and Appendix B is reordered. The main section progression and most method, proof, and existing supplementary-analysis prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds colored-data and video figures, redesigns the AFHQ and several ImageNet/LDM displays, and relocates numerous main-text figures into the appendix. The LDM higher-frequency display changes from three mode rows to two, although its caption still says top-three. Table 1 is relocated with unchanged contents.

improvement.justification: The controlled novelty checks in Section 5.2 provide clearer validation, while code/hardware disclosures and targeted mathematical corrections improve verifiability. The video experiment adds useful applicability evidence. These gains are limited by predominantly qualitative validation, removal of v1 Figure 3's frequency/uncertainty summaries, and inconsistent AFHQ sample-count reporting. Overall, the evidence supports a modest quality improvement.
